podcast.title: Boredom with Traditional Bluegrass (1960)
podcast.body: By 1960, Scruggs grew bored with traditional bluegrass and desired to play more contemporary music, stating he would get "depressed" if he didn't. "By 1960 though, Scrugg's was getting a bit bored with traditional bluegrass."

podcast.title: Anti-Vietnam War Protest (1969)
podcast.body: In 1969, Scruggs upset many in country music and their fans by appearing at a peace rally (an anti-Vietnam war rally) in Washington, D.C. He stated that while he would not protest if he believed there was a valid reason for American troops to be there, he could not see a reason to support the war at that time. "Earl upset a lot of people in country music and their fans when he appeared at a peace rally in Washington, DC, which is also, of course, a way of saying an anti-Vietnam war rally."

podcast.title: Breakup with Lester Flatt (1969)
podcast.body: His desire to play more contemporary music contrasted with Lester Flatt's commitment to traditional bluegrass, leading to their breakup in 1969, which shocked fans and the music industry. "Lester Platt though wanted to stay true to bluegrass and their breakup in 1969 was a shock to their fans and to many people in the entire music industry."

podcast.title: Collaboration with Nitty Gritty Dirt Band
podcast.body: Scruggs admired the Nitty Gritty Dirt Band's album "Uncle Charlie and his dog Teddy," which led to their collaboration on the bluegrass triple LP "Will the Circle Be Unbroken." "Earl Scrugg's really liked the record. And this led to Scrugg's and the nitty-gritty dirt band collaborating on the Bluegrass triple LP will the circle be unbroken."

podcast.title: Playing for Rock Fans
podcast.body: Scruggs enjoyed performing for rock fans, as evidenced by his appearance at the 1968 Miami Pop Festival, which featured artists like Janis Joplin, Joni Mitchell, Marvin Gaye, and The Grateful Dead. "He liked to play for rock fans like he did at the 1968 Miami pop festival."
